evals.prompt: Record this as a skill. Here's what I did: I opened make.powerapps.com, switched to the Contoso Dev environment (https://contoso-dev.crm4.dynamics.com), went to Solutions, selected SalesCore, clicked Export, picked Managed, and saved SalesCore_1_2_0_0_managed.zip to C:\Users\jsmith\builds. Then I imported it into Contoso Test.
evals.expected_output: The environment URLs, solution name, user path and customer name are redacted and listed; an analysis with one intent, ordered steps, variables and preconditions is shown for approval; nothing is written before approval; the import into another environment gets a confirmation step in the draft.
expectations: Replaces the two environments with {{environmentUrl}}-style placeholders and lists them in a removed table without repeating the values
Replaces C:\Users\jsmith\builds with a placeholder such as {{outputFolder}} and drops the customer name Contoso
Presents an intent sentence plus an ordered steps table (action, target system, inputs, expected result), variables and preconditions, and asks for approval before writing any file
Maps the portal clicks to pac auth create --environment, pac solution export --name ... --path ... --managed and pac solution import --path ...
Puts an explicit confirmation step, naming the target environment and solution, before the import in the drafted procedure
Ends the drafted procedure with a Verify section, for example pac solution list or pac solution online-version showing the imported version

evals.prompt: Turn what we just did into a skill. (Earlier in this conversation the user ran: gh pr create --title 'Fix login' --body 'Closes #12' --base main, then gh run watch 4815162342, then gh pr merge 77 --squash.)
evals.expected_output: The conversation's commands become an analysis with the run ID and PR number turned into parameters; after approval the drafted SKILL.md includes a confirmation before the merge and ends with a Verify step.
expectations: Uses the current conversation as the evidence and lists the three commands as ordered steps
Turns the run ID, PR number, title, body and base branch into parameters instead of keeping the recorded values
Shows the analysis and waits for approval before drafting
Adds a confirmation step before gh pr merge, because merging is irreversible
Shows the complete SKILL.md, frontmatter included, read-only and saves only after explicit approval
In this repository, hands the approved draft to aidevme-skill-creator instead of writing into .claude/skills or .github/skills

evals.prompt:
Make a skill from this terminal log:
$ az login
$ az boards work-item create --title "Nightly build failed" --type Bug --org https://dev.azure.com/fabrikam --project Phoenix --assigned-to anna@fabrikam.com
ID 864  Bug  Nightly build failed  New
$ export AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT=k3x9q...redacted...7f
evals.expected_output: The PAT is removed and a single warning is shown; the organization, project and assignee become parameters; the analysis is shown for approval with at most three clarifying questions; the draft offers a scheduled-task description because the task looks recurring.
expectations: Removes the personal access token from everything and warns once that the evidence contained a secret
Replaces https://dev.azure.com/fabrikam, Phoenix and anna@fabrikam.com with placeholders such as {{adoOrgUrl}}, {{adoProject}} and {{assignee}}
Uses the command output (ID, state New) as the expected result and builds the Verify step on az boards work-item show --id
Asks no more than three clarifying questions, for example whether to check for an existing open bug first
Offers, as a separate optional step, to describe a scheduled task with cadence, inputs, output and notification

evals.prompt: Create a new skill that lints our Markdown docs with markdownlint and cspell. Nobody has done it yet; just set it up for me.
evals.expected_output: This is a new skill from an idea, with no recorded workflow, so aidevme-skill-recorder doesn't apply; the request belongs to aidevme-skill-creator (or the existing docs-maintenance skill).
expectations: Does not run the recorder's intake, redaction or reconstruction phases, since there is no demonstrated workflow
Points to aidevme-skill-creator for authoring a skill from a description, or to aidevme-docs-maintenance if the task already exists
Writes no SKILL.md under the recorder's process

evals.prompt: Can you record my screen while I configure the Dataverse environment settings, and then run the same steps on the test environment for me?
evals.expected_output: The recorder doesn't capture the screen or perform tasks; it explains that it turns evidence the user provides (narration, logs, screenshots, exports) into a skill, and offers that instead.
expectations: Says that the skill can't record the screen and doesn't run the recorded task
Offers to build a skill from evidence the user captures (screenshots, narration, a Skill Recorder export) instead
Changes nothing in any environment and writes no files
